entries.note: Imai 2013 PNAS resolves (PMID 23918359, epub 2013-08-05); quote verbatim in the abstract. Untested opener at model_first_use_year 2013 is right; no antibody binds mouse IL-33, product_in_model false correct.

Smith 2017 PLoS Genet resolves (PMID 28273074); quote verbatim in abstract. Phenotype is asthma/eosinophils; full-text check for an AD phenotype timed out, not verified. Track opening 2017 here vs model_first_use_year 2012 is tolerable.

Chen 2019 STM resolves (PMID 31645451); quote verbatim, abstract only (paywalled). Direction-only same holds. Field fix: product_in_model must be false (etokimab never dosed in mice; entry 1 says so). No CT.gov record of the 12-patient study found.
Same source, quote verbatim in abstract. Placebo-controlled HDM challenge inside the dosed-patient study: comparison_stated true, own human_challenge track, downstream readout all correct.

Smith 2017 eosinophil prediction vs Chen 2019 eosinophil fall is admissible on direction. product_in_model has no meaning on a human_genetic track: set false. Would drop confidence to low (12 patients, no placebo for eosinophils).

Kosloski 2024 CTS resolves (PMID 39077906, OA); quote verbatim. NCT03738423 results (2022-06-10) post functional-itepekimab PK only, no total IL-33 or eosinophils, so 2024 is the first date for this datum. strengthens on same-to-same is outside #127 (rule question).
Salimi 2013 JEM resolves (PMID 24323357, OA); quote verbatim. Untested opener: no mouse source states an antibody exposure target; product_in_model false correct.

Hirota 2012 Nat Genet resolves (PMID 23042114, epub 2012-10-07); quote is the abstract clause with ellipses, near-verbatim. Admissible human_genetic opener; causal gene unresolved across IL1RL1/IL18R1/IL18RAP (rule question).
Salimi 2013 quote verbatim. Li 2017 (10.1038/cddis.2017.90, PMID 28383552) resolves and carries the quoted therapeutic-target sentence in its abstract. Mouse-track opener correct.

Release scraped, dated Nov. 08, 2019, quote verbatim. NCT03533751 results 2023-05-24: LS-mean differences 7.75/-6.32/1.97/4.82, p 0.45-0.83, placebo -49.4%, as stated. Pietka 2020 cites NCT03533751 as motivation: retro entry belongs here (see missing). 8-K date unverified.
Quote verbatim in abstract. Open-label EASI arm plus placebo-controlled challenge; untested opener on the human_challenge track in the same year with the model entry first (#30) is correct.
Same release and registry record as entry 3. Contra on this track holds: the 83% EASI50 arm had no placebo and ATLAS placebo fell 49%. Separate track from the mouse is right (different system).

Drafter's pairing; contra on direction is admissible for a human_genetic track (decision 8) at low confidence. Hirota's locus does not resolve to IL33/IL1RL1 and Smith 2017 is an asthma finding, so untested is the alternative (rule question). product_in_model false.

Status right, year wrong: the second miss was public 2021-04-20 (NCT03831191 results, 'terminated for lack of efficacy after an interim analysis'), then NCT03736967 2021-11-01. Torudokimab's tier-1 report Laquer 2022 BJD (10.1111/bjd.21631, epub 2022-07-29) is missing from patient_trials (doi null).
entries.adjudication_note: Both agree contra (second miss on a failed track, strengthens). Rule 6: year is the earliest public date of that second miss, NCT03831191 results 2021-04-20, not Kosloski 2024; add Laquer 2022 DOI to patient_trials.

entries.note: Okragly 2021 J Inflamm Res resolves (PMID 34408465, OA); quote verbatim. Abstract also states no binding to mouse, rat or rabbit IL-33 and cyno cross-reactivity engineered for unpublished NHP toxicity studies. Specificity panel is in vitro; model_kind rests on cyno PK.

Model side is torudokimab-specific (specificity, cyno PK), an off-target prediction that does not pool across members (decision 12); pair with torudokimab's own record, NCT03831191 AE table (2021-04-20; SAEs 0/33, 0/35, 0/34, 2/33) or Laquer 2022, not itepekimab. Low confidence; else untested.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 5 no_prediction: a binding-specificity panel plus cyno PK names no harm and states no margin, so nothing checkable; 'clean antibody' is the drafter's inference. Torudokimab data also cannot predict itepekimab's tolerability.

entries.note: Peng 2018 resolves (PMID 28952069; Crossref online 2017-09-26, print Feb 2018); quote verbatim, abstract only. Untested opener at 2017 correct under rule 7. Missed pairing: Chen 2019 full text reports no serum-IgE change in 12 dosed patients (see missing).

Okragly 2021 resolves (PMID 34408465, PMC8364917, epub 2021-08-11); quote verbatim; full text: torudokimab 1 day before human IL-33 i.p., serum IL-5 at 6 h, n=5. Untested holds. Rule 7 proxy would allow a 2017 opener (paper dates FIH to Nov 2017); status unchanged.

Chen 2019 resolves (PMID 31645451; ORA accepted manuscript read). Quote verbatim. Opener fine, but the system is healthy-donor neutrophils migrating to patients' blister fluid in transwells, run after the trial readout; see index 10. Study is EudraCT 2016-002539-14.

Full text: 'Given the clinical trial data implicating a key role for IL-33 in granulocyte migration in vivo, we next tested whether etokimab could modulate neutrophil migration ex vivo', on trial blister fluid; inhibition partial (Fig. 7C). Motivated by the patient result: retro, retrodiction true.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 10: the transwell assay ran on trial blister fluid after, and 'given', the in-vivo neutrophil result, so it is a retrodiction; it reproduces the human direction (partial inhibition), hence retro, never same. retrodiction: true.

entries.note: Peng 2018 resolves; quote verbatim in abstract (14 s.c. doses over 33 days, tacrolimus comparator confirmed there). Crossref online 2017-09-26, PubMed entrez 2017-09-28, print Feb 2018: year 2017 is right under rule 7. Untested opener correct.

Release scraped (Nov. 08, 2019), quote verbatim; NCT03533751 results 2023-05-24: LS-mean differences 7.75/-6.32/1.97/4.82, p 0.45-0.83, placebo -49.38%. Model predicted cure, patients no benefit: contra; tier 5 with model_src tier 1 per decision 2. Same src/tier question as efficacy 3.

NCT03831191 read via API v2: whyStopped verbatim, results first posted 2021-04-20, vIGA 0/1 9.5/5.0/5.9/4.8%. Second miss on the track, strengthens per #127; year 2021 under rule 7, consistent with the correction on efficacy 7.

DaSilva-Arnold 2018 resolves (PMID 29368135, PMC6198812, epub 2018-01-24); quote verbatim; full text: modified-EASI scores higher or trending higher at every week 10-20, n=11/group. Untested opener at 2018 correct; the stated prediction is worsening (IL-33 attenuates), not a null.

Model predicted worsening; ATLAS arms moved with placebo (differences +7.8 to -6.3, p 0.45-0.83). Null-null is same only when the null was predicted (#58); here the predicted effect was absent, which decision 4 calls failed. Contra at low confidence; same would set the cell headline matched.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 (#58): the model predicted worsening, not a null, and that effect was absent (arms tracked placebo); null-null is same only when the null was predicted. Decision 5 analogue: a conservative model is still wrong. magnitude: opposite.

entries.note: Chen 2019 accepted manuscript (ORA uuid:5e031a33-1e4d...) quote verbatim: IgE 10101/9954/10321 kU/L, day 0/29/140. Peng 2018 abstract (online 2017-09-26): aIL-33Ab significantly reduced serum IgE in DNCB mice. Contra low confidence holds; Chen attributes the null to nothing.

missing: Peng 2018 (Inflammation, doi 10.1007/s10753-017-0673-7, PMID 28952069): anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice, 'blockade of IL-33 has a curative effect on AD' (abstract). A prospective pharmacological track (sibling antibody, product_in_model false) that predicted efficacy and was contradicted by ATLAS 2019; no track in the draft. The same paper also correlates serum IL-33/sST2 with human AD activity (comparison_stated in-source).

Pietka 2020 (Sci Rep, doi 10.1038/s41598-020-63410-z, PMID 32296080) as a retro entry on il33-st2-mouse-dermatitis, year 2020: received 2020-01-28, its introduction cites the NCT03533751 failure ('the fate of IL-33 inhibition in atopic dermatitis is therefore highly questionable'), and IL-33-/-, ST2-/- and double-knockout mice develop MC903 dermatitis like wild type. Decision 10 draws it on its track with retrodiction: true, not only in judgement.

DaSilva-Arnold 2018 (Arch Dermatol Res, doi 10.1007/s00403-018-1807-y, PMID 29368135, epub 2018-01-24): Stat6VT AD mice, 'AD-like disease was more severe in IL-33-deficient Stat6VT mice ... IL-33 may attenuate inflammation in this system'. A prospective pre-ATLAS model predicting no benefit (if anything harm) from IL-33 loss; candidate track scored same/partial on direction (no benefit seen, no worsening) or untested.

Okragly 2021 (doi 10.2147/JIR.S320287): torudokimab's own in vivo human-IL-33-induced pharmacodynamic inhibition assay in mice (IL-5 endpoint), a member drug's engagement model never compared with patient PD; an untested engagement track distinct from the cyno specificity/PK safety track.

Chen 2019 (doi 10.1126/scitranslmed.aax2945): 'etokimab also inhibited neutrophil migration to skin interstitial fluid in vitro', an ex_vivo human system compared in-source with the in vivo HDM challenge; candidate separate ex_vivo engagement track (same, comparison_stated true) rather than folded into the human_challenge track.

Laquer 2022 (Br J Dermatol, doi 10.1111/bjd.21631, PMID 35481678, epub 2022-07-29; Lilly authors incl. Okragly, Sims): tier-1 report of the torudokimab AD trial, 'Interleukin-33 antibody failed to demonstrate benefit in a phase II ... study'. Not a model, but a missed source: patient_trials NCT03831191 has doi null. No abstract (research letter); not opened, paywalled.

Checked and not applicable: England 2023 (Sci Rep, doi 10.1038/s41598-023-36642-y) tozorakimab characterization uses primary human cells and a murine lung epithelial-injury model, no skin or AD system; Imai 2019 (JID, 10.1016/j.jid.2019.04.016) is the same K14-IL-33 transgenic track already opened by Imai 2013.

models: Peng 2018 serum-IgE readout vs Chen 2019 full text (ORA accepted manuscript, https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:5e031a33-1e4d-4f51-b2e7-3c4001ee8f4d): 'There was no significant change in serum total IgE during the study (mean total serum IgE at study entry 10101+7594 kU/L; day 29 post-etokimab 9954+7394 kU/L; day 140 post-etokimab 10321+8103 kU/L)'. A missed engagement pairing on anti-il33-mab-dncb-mouse-ad: the model predicted serum IgE falls, 12 dosed AD patients showed none at day 29/140, while peripheral eosinophils fell 40% (lesional in the model). Candidate contra or same + partial, year 2019, low confidence (single open-label 300 mg dose, no placebo arm for IgE).

engagement, anti-il33-mab-dncb-mouse-ad: Kosloski 2024 (doi:10.1111/cts.13874) itepekimab AD PK/PD with repeated q2w/q4w dosing may report serum total IgE; a secondary listing says IgE reductions were 'more gradual'. Not confirmed it was itepekimab vs placebo; if so, a later same entry on this track.
could_not_verify: Smith 2017 full text for an atopic dermatitis phenotype of rs146597587 (Europe PMC full-text fetch timed out; not retried).
The AnaptysBio 8-K exhibit 99.2 filing date (EDGAR full-text search returned 403); the release itself is dated Nov. 08, 2019 and carries the quote verbatim.
Any registry record for the 12-patient Chen 2019 etokimab study (CT.gov lists only NCT03533751, NCT02920021, NCT03469934, NCT03614923, NCT04256044 for ANB020/etokimab).
Laquer 2022 BJD content beyond title and author list.
An earlier sponsor (tier 5) disclosure of the itepekimab AD discontinuation before the 2021-11-01 NCT03736967 results posting (Firecrawl search surfaced none).
rule_questions: A tier-5 press release dates the entry (2019) while a tier-3 registry record (2023-05-24) sets the status: which document is `src`/`source_tier`, and does `trial_unreported` stay true once a registry results record exists?

Decision 10 vs decision 6: may a `retro` entry be appended to a track already `contra` (Pietka 2020 on the IL-33/ST2 knockout MC903 track), and does a same-system re-run that overturns the model's earlier result count as the model 'reproducing the human data' or as a model-replication failure?

Decision 7 when the registry results record lacks the datum the comparison rests on (NCT03738423 posts functional PK only; total-IL-33 saturation and eosinophils first appear in Kosloski 2024): does the registry date still set `year` for the dose and engagement entries?

Is a GWAS locus shared by three receptor genes (IL1RL1-IL18R1-IL18RAP) with the causal gene unresolved an admissible class prediction for anti-IL-33 (`contra`) or `untested`; and what does `product_in_model` mean on a human_genetic track?

Safety: can a member-specific specificity panel plus cyno PK (torudokimab) be paired with another member's tolerability (itepekimab) when decision 12 pools only on-target harms; and is a specificity statement a 'stated prediction' of no harm at all, or is the cell `untested`?
#127 defines `strengthens: true` for a second miss; is it allowed on a same-to-same engagement entry (Kosloski 2024 direct readout), or should that datum go in `patient_trials`?

models: efficacy, a prospective model whose stated prediction was worsening (DaSilva-Arnold: IL-33 attenuates Stat6VT disease) when patients showed a null (ATLAS arms ~ placebo): same on the no-benefit half (direction_only), contra by #58/decision 4 (predicted effect absent), or an efficacy analogue of decision 5's over-prediction? Under decision 6 the answer sets the tile's efficacy headline.

models: decision 10 for an ex-vivo assay inside the trial paper itself, run after and 'given the clinical trial data' (Chen 2019 transwells on trial blister fluid): retro as proposed, and does a track that only ever retrodicted still open with an untested entry (#30/#112)?

models: rule 7 proxy dating for a candidate-selection PD assay published four years after first-in-human (Okragly 2021; FIH Nov 2017): open the untested strip at publication (2021, as the draft's cyno track) or at first class use with the paper as proxy (2017)?

engagement 11: the DNCB model dosed antibody 14 times over 33 days; Chen gave one 300 mg dose. Is a single-dose null on a slow-turnover readout (IgE) a contra, or untested because the dosing regimen differs from the model's?
